title: Continuous Measurement of Biological Noise in Escherichia Coli Using Time-lapse Microscopy
protocol: Weigh 0.5 g of carbenicillin.
Add 10 mL of sterile H2O.
Dissolve completely.
Sterilize the solution through a 0.22 µm syringe filter.
Aliquot and store the antibiotic solution at -20°C.
Mix 5 g of tryptone, 5 g of NaCl, 2.5 g of yeast extract, and 7.5 g of Bacto agar with 0.5 L of sterile H2O.
Autoclave the LB solution at 121 °C for 20 min.
Partially submerge the molten gel-mix in a 50 °C water bath.
Add 1,000 µL of carbenicillin (50 mg/mL) to the molten agar mix.
Pour the mixture into Petri dishes under sterile conditions.
Allow the plates to set before storing them in the fridge.
Prepare separate stock solutions for 5x M9 salts (56.4 g/L), 2 M glucose, and 2% biotin-free casamino acids.
Autoclave each solution at 121 °C for 20 min.
Mix 1125 mg of low melting agar and 400 mg of agar with 89.2 mL of minimal media (1x M9).
Add 10 mL of 2% casamino acids to the mixture in a 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask.
Pour the media on the inner lips of the flask.
Microwave the solution in short bursts until it is clear and not boiling.
Place the flask in a hot water bath (60 °C) for further mixing by diffusion.
Cool the solution to about 45-50°C.
Light the flame at the plate-pouring bench.
Add quickly all solutions in the following order: 800 µL of 50% glycerol (0.4% [vol/vol]), 100 µL of thiamine (B1), 1100 µL of Glucose (2M), and 100 µL of Carbenicillin (50 mg/mL).
Swirl the Erlenmeyer flask to ensure even distribution.
Open one plate at a time next to the flame and begin pouring.
Leave the plates on the bench for a few minutes until initial solidification.
Turn the plates upside down to prevent water condensation from dripping onto the gel.
Leave the plates to solidify at room temperature for about 2 h.
Once the plates have solidified and dried, store them at 4 °C for about 3 months.
Transform the desired plasmid into Escherichia coli MG1655 cells with the standard heat shock protocol.
Grow the transformed cells on an LB agar plate overnight at 37°C.
Inoculate a single colony into 5 mL of LB broth supplemented with relevant antibiotics.
Grow cells at 37 °C with 250 rpm shaking speed in an incubator for 2 h until liquid is cloudy.
Mix 892 µL of minimal media (1x M9) with 8 µL of 50% glycerol, 100 µL of 2% Casamino acids, 1 µL of thiamine (B1), and 11 µL of Glucose (2 M).
Add 1 µL of relevant antibiotics to the mixture.
Spin down the prepared dilution solution.
Dilute the cell culture from step 2.4 in a 2 mL tube by adding 30 µL of Escherichia coli growth to 1000 µL of dilution solution.
Incubate the tube for 1 h with shaking (250 rpm) at 37 °C.
Grow 40 µL - 60 µL on M9 plates prepared in step 1.10.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C overnight.
Prepare three microscope plates by repeating steps 2.3 to 2.6 for colonies from plate prepared at step 2.9 microscope measurements.
Preheat a water bath to 60 °C.
Mix 112.5 mg of low melting agar with 40 mg of agar and 8.92 mL of minimal media (1x M9).
Add 1 mL of 2% Casamino acids to the mixture in a 25 mL Erlenmeyer flask.
Microwave the solution in short bursts of 2 to 3 seconds until clear.
Place the 25 mL Erlenmeyer flask in a hot water bath at 60°C.
Wipe the outside of the flask clean and leave it to cool until its temperature falls to about 45-50°C.
Clean the bench with 70% ethanol.
Stretch tape on the cleaned bench, ensuring it is smooth and leveled.
Prepare two coverslips: one on the tape and a second nearby.
Prepare a coverlid.
Mix quickly all solutions in the following order:
80 µL of 50% glycerol (0.4% [vol/vol]).
1 mL of 2% casamino acids (0.2% [wt/vol]).
10 µL of thiamine (B1).
110 µL of glucose (2 M).
10 µL of relevant antibiotics.
Pour 1.5 mL of the gel on the coverslip and cover it with the second piece to make a "sandwich".
Return the Erlenmeyer flask to the hot water bath.
Cover the sandwich with the lid and set timer for 20 minutes.
Incubate the tube from step 2.11 for 1 h at 37°C with shaking (250 rpm).
After 20 minutes, flip the sandwich and cover it again.
Leave the "sandwich" to rest for 1 hour.
Seed Escherichia coli culture by pipetting the sample onto a 35 mm dish.
Pipette 6 μL of cells as separate small drops.
Allow the cell drops to dry for at least 15 minutes and up to 30 minutes.
Slide the coverslip away to expose the solidified gel from the sandwich preparation.
Cut the sandwich into small individual pads using a biopsy punch or tip.
Lean the cut pads gently onto the sample.
Leave the dish on the bench for 20 minutes.
Remove the flask from the water bath about 3 minutes before the timer ends.
Pour 3 mL of the gel constantly to the plate perimeter in a circular motion.
Seal plates with tape and pierce several holes with a 25 G needle.
Flip all the dishes to prevent water condensation dripping onto the gel.
Incubate all dishes at 4 °C for 30 minutes to allow full solidification while preventing cell mitosis.
Store samples at 4 °C for successive measurements, no more than one day.
Start the microscope according to manufacturer instructions.
Find the initial focus using the lowest amplification lens.
Engage the automatic focus system (AFS).
Use oil if needed by drowning the lens with oil and spreading it carefully without manual movement of the plate.
Use relative cross-section in Z direction following default suggestions for Z step cross-sections.
Take bright field images every 5 minutes.
Take fluorescent images every 20 minutes.
Adjust focus during the first 30 minutes if necessary.
Preheat the microscope incubator box and oil.
Refrigerate the sample to help reduce initial loss of focus.
Define the folder of acquisition images in main_code.m.
Define the image time period for bright field channel time step in minutes.
Define the GFP frequency - rate of acquisition of GFP images.
Define the microscope resolution (how many pixels equal 1 µm).
Define histogram bin range for cell area.
Run main_code.m, which will run all other scripts automatically (count_cells.m, cell_growth_rate.m).
Program automatically segments bright field images (see Supplementary Figure 2-4).
Combine the segmentation image with fluorescent image (GFP) to extract intensity level per cell.
Calculate the graph of amount of cells by time and fit according to exponential growth.
Calculate the mean and standard deviation (STD) for each cell area range.
Calculate the signal to noise ratio (SNR) for each cell area range.
Plot and fit the distribution of amount of cells by intensity.
Calculate the coefficient of Variance (CV) and compare to flow analyzer data.
